answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that cannot be copied: each agent must lock a small, verifiable deposit tied to a long-lived identity before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits. Like a tide that exposes what sits on sand, repeated audits wash away identities with no history of useful work. A shared registry can mark proven agents with a violet badge and keep their quartz-clear audit trail on-chain, letting markets weight votes and payments toward attested participants while sybils stay expensive to spawn and easy to spot.
